messages:
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Cc: Emma Lowe <emma@acme.com>
Date: Fri, 15 Jun 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: XFN bridge & decision cadence — QBR prep and exec asks

Team —

Thanks for jumping in on yesterday's bridge. I pulled together a short list of outstanding exec asks and decisions we need to lock before the QBR readout to Acme next week. High level: pricing guardrails for enterprise tier, final model selection for low-latency endpoint, and the mutual action plan signoff with Procurement.

Quick asks:
- Lauren: confirm the two candidate pricing bands and the preferred recommendation to present to Emma by EOD Tue (18 Jun).
- Marissa: ownership on the rollout timeline slides and a one-slide risk summary for the QBR.
- Karthik: confirm compute/infra constraints if we propose the lower-latency variant (estimate p50/p95 impact).
- Vivek: capture any runbook or SLA exceptions we should disclose to Acme and wash through legal.

I'm attaching the current QBR deck and the M.A.P. draft for Procurement. Please comment inline on Acme_Mutual_Action_Plan.xlsx and I will combine changes on Monday.

Attachments: [Attachment: QBR_Roadmap_Slides_v2.pdf (pdf)], [Attachment: Acme_Mutual_Action_Plan.xlsx (xlsx)]

Sergio Alvarez
VP, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>

Date: Sun, 17 Jun 2028 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: XFN bridge & decision cadence — QBR prep and exec asks

On Fri, Jun 15, 2028 at 09:12 AM Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.com> wrote:
> Team —
> 
> Thanks for jumping in on yesterday's bridge...

Thanks — quick clarifications below:

- Pricing: I ran two scenarios with finance (net-net): 1) Standard enterprise band (list+15% discount range) and 2) Accelerated adoption band (higher initial discount, steeper ramp). My recommendation is scenario 2 for the first 12 months but with a committed-minimum to protect unit economics. I'll attach the short P&L snippet to the MAP comments.
- Slides: I'll take the roadmap timeline and add the commit milestones (canaries, dedicated ramp dates) by Mon EOD.

Action: I'll post the P&L snippet to the MAP file and ping Sergio when done. Emma — want to make sure Procurement sees the committed-minimum language; happy to sync 20m on Monday if helpful.

-Lauren
Director, GTM Strategy
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Thanks — status update:

- Roadmap slide: draft with milestone swimlane uploaded to the QBR deck (see slide 4). I flagged the canary window and the dedicated pool start date.
- Risk slide: short summary ready; three bullets (1. infra delta if low-latency variant chosen, 2. potential data residency ask from Acme EU teams, 3. procurement negotiation on commit minimum).
- MAP: added two rows for next steps and owners (Lauren = pricing, Marissa = slides, Sergio = exec alignment).

Notes to Sergio: I'll call out the mitigation plan for the infra delta — we can present a fallback: downgrade to the compatible quantized variant with a clearly stated latency delta and cost delta.

Attachments referenced inline; no binary changes.

Marissa Cole
Senior PM, Customer Success
Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: XFN bridge & decision cadence — QBR prep and exec asks

Quick check-in: infra numbers for the low-latency variant — rough p50 change +8ms, p95 +22ms on current fleet; cost uplift ~18% on tokens due to dedicated NVMe caching and increased batch throughput. If we keep the default batching and prefix caching it's more like +4ms/+10ms and ~8% cost. Happy to walk through the infra slide Tuesday.

I'll add the microbench table to the shared doc (under the MAP comments).

Karthik Iyer
Head of Inference Ops
Redwood Inference
